name: ELI5
instruction: Write for a curious child: very simple words, one idea at a time and an everyday comparison, because the person wants the core intuition with no background needed. Stay accurate while simplifying.
effect: Very simple vocabulary and an everyday comparison

name: Layperson
instruction: Write for an intelligent reader with no background in the field: define each technical term when it first appears and give the context they would be missing.
effect: Technical terms defined on first use

name: Expert-level
instruction: Write for an expert in the field: use precise technical vocabulary freely and skip the basics, because the person already knows them and wants depth.
effect: Technical vocabulary without definitions; no basics

name: Decision-maker
meaning: Someone who needs the bottom line to act
example: Written for a decision-maker with 2 minutes
instruction: Write for a busy decision-maker: lead with the decision or recommendation, then the key trade-offs, costs and risks, because they need to act on it within minutes.
effect: Opens with a recommendation, then trade-offs and risks

name: Skeptic
instruction: Write for a reader who doubts the claim: lead with evidence, address the obvious objections, and name the weakest point yourself, because they will look for it.
effect: Evidence first, objections addressed, weakest point named
